# Export resume review

Arun reviewed the accepted export resume design during a solo working session. The design uses signed client offsets and frames the accepted export-retries problem, whose constraints include account isolation, existing downloads and retention limits.

Arun found that signed client offsets make revocation difficult and favors investigating opaque account-bound tokens. This is an investigative preference: no replacement design or decision has been approved. The existing design already calls for reconsideration if revocation cannot be enforced; the concern warrants review but does not establish that enforcement is impossible.

Proxy handling of range requests remains unresolved in the open proxy-range inquiry. No prototype result is available. Arun wants to revisit the existing design after that inquiry.

## Implications and open questions

The revocation concern implicates `2026-10-02-export-resume`. A future token proposal could supersede that accepted design while retaining `2026-10-01-export-retries-problem` as its frame. The account-isolation, compatibility and retention constraints still apply; this session did not invalidate the problem framing.

The proxy question is already tracked by `2026-10-03-proxy-range`; a duplicate inquiry is unnecessary. Questions remain about supported proxy behavior and whether opaque tokens can provide enforceable revocation within the existing constraints.

## Follow-up choices

Arun can choose to continue the existing proxy inquiry, then revisit the accepted design once evidence is available. The execution owner and timing have not been assigned.

Arun can choose `propose-design` to investigate an opaque-token successor that frames the existing problem and supersedes the accepted design. This note does not approve or create that design.

If a design choice is reached later, Arun can choose `record-decision` with a link to the resulting design. No decision or status transition follows from this session alone.
